--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[EVT-1] Idempotency keyed to projectId causes event loss
File: src/inngest/functions.ts (L70-L220)
Evidence: Both generateReverseArchitectureFunction and regenerateReverseArchitectureFunction set idempotency to 'event.data.projectId', which will collapse distinct push/regenerate events for the same project into a single processed event. This misuses idempotency for events that differ by commit SHA/afterCommit so unique pushes are silently deduplicated.
Impact: On a 10x spike of pushes to the same repo, many distinct commits will be dropped/unprocessed (lost async work) instead of queued, causing missing architecture updates. 
Fix: Use a commit-unique idempotency key (e.g., commit SHA or delivery id) or include both projectId+afterCommit for idempotency so each distinct push is processed.

[EVT-2] Expensive generation has no idempotency/backpressure
File: src/inngest/functions.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: generateArchitectureFunction comments and code indicate a 5–10 minute CPU/IO-heavy operation but it has no idempotency key and no producer-side throttling. The function throws on errors (delegating retries to Inngest) without coalescing or rate limits.
Impact: A 10x burst of generate-architecture events will queue many long-running jobs, causing unbounded backlog, duplicated heavy work, consumer lag, and large cost spikes. 
Fix: Add idempotency (e.g., generationId or user+context), enforce producer rate-limits/coalescing, and gate concurrent executions per user/project.

[EVT-3] Webhook enqueues unthrottled Inngest tasks for Pro users
File: src/app/api/webhook/github/route.ts (L200-L420)
Evidence: On push events for Pro users the webhook directly calls inngest.send({ name: "reverse-architecture/regenerate", data: ... }) with no rate limiting, batching, or backpressure; free users instead store a single pending commit. 
Impact: A 10x push spike from CI or many contributors will flood Inngest with expensive regenerate jobs, causing queue saturation

--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[EVT-1] Idempotency keyed to projectId causes event loss
File: src/inngest/functions.ts (L70-L220)
Evidence: Both generateReverseArchitectureFunction and regenerateReverseArchitectureFunction set idempotency to 'event.data.projectId', which will collapse distinct push/regenerate events for the same project into a single processed event. This misuses idempotency for events that differ by commit SHA/afterCommit so unique pushes are silently deduplicated.
Impact: On a 10x spike of pushes to the same repo, many distinct commits will be dropped/unprocessed (lost async work) instead of queued, causing missing architecture updates. 
Fix: Use a commit-unique idempotency key (e.g., commit SHA or delivery id) or include both projectId+afterCommit for idempotency so each distinct push is processed.

[EVT-2] Expensive generation has no idempotency/backpressure
File: src/inngest/functions.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: generateArchitectureFunction comments and code indicate a 5–10 minute CPU/IO-heavy operation but it has no idempotency key and no producer-side throttling. The function throws on errors (delegating retries to Inngest) without coalescing or rate limits.
Impact: A 10x burst of generate-architecture events will queue many long-running jobs, causing unbounded backlog, duplicated heavy work, consumer lag, and large cost spikes. 
Fix: Add idempotency (e.g., generationId or user+context), enforce producer rate-limits/coalescing, and gate concurrent executions per user/project.

[EVT-3] Webhook enqueues unthrottled Inngest tasks for Pro users
File: src/app/api/webhook/github/route.ts (L200-L420)
Evidence: On push events for Pro users the webhook directly calls inngest.send({ name: "reverse-architecture/regenerate", data: ... }) with no rate limiting, batching, or backpressure; free users instead store a single pending commit. 
Impact: A 10x push spike from CI or many contributors will flood Inngest with expensive regenerate jobs, causing queue saturation, slowdowns, and retry storms if downstream transient errors occur. 
Fix: Apply per-repo/user rate limits, debounce/coalesce frequent pushes (enqueue only latest commit), or route to a durable throttled queue that limits concurrent regenerations.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[EVT-4] No DLQ or explicit failure/exhausted-retry handling
File: src/inngest/functions.ts (L1-L400)
Evidence: Functions throw errors to let Inngest retry but there are no explicit onFailure handlers, dead-letter writes, or alerts for exhausted retries; failures are logged only via console.error. 
Impact: Poison messages or persistent failures during a 10x spike can repeatedly retry or be silently dropped, increasing load and hiding lost events. 
Fix: Add onFailure/step failure handlers to persist failures to a DLQ table, emit alerts, and surface retry counts.

[EVT-5] Free-user pending commit state overwrites previous data
File: src/app/api/webhook/github/route.ts (L300-L420)
Evidence: For non-Pro users the webhook updates project.pendingCommitData to the latest commit, overwriting any prior pendingCommitData rather than enqueuing or recording multiple updates. 
Impact: Under frequent pushes (10x spike) intermediate pushes are lost (coalesced without trace), causing missed regenerations and potential user confusion. 
Fix: Replace single-slot pendingCommitData with a queued store (append or upsert by commit) or a coalescing queue that preserves the newest and records skipped commits.

--- INFO ---

[EVT-6] Webhook deduplication using github delivery id
File: src/app/api/webhook/github/route.ts (L80-L120)
Evidence: The webhook upserts db.webhookEvent using the GitHub delivery header to dedupe duplicate deliveries, which prevents immediate duplicate processing.
